fullDesc: In May 1997 IBM's Deep Blue beat world champion Garry Kasparov 3.5 to 2.5 in a six-game match in New York. It was the first time a reigning champion lost a match to a computer under standard conditions.
realFacts: Kasparov had beaten an earlier version in 1996
IBM dismantled Deep Blue after the match
Today's phone chess programs are stronger
